Class HttpApplication

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.http.server.HttpApplication
public final class HttpApplication extends Object
Starts an HTTP application whose routes are declared in code, typically in the main method.

The routes are functional routes, registered as HttpRoutes beans. They coexist with the controllers and beans of the application, which are discovered as for Micronaut.run(String...).

public static void main(String[] args) {
    HttpApplication.run(args, routes ->
        routes.GET("/hello/{name}", (request, vars) -> HttpResponse.ok("Hello " + vars.getString("name"))));
}

Routes that need application beans receive a BeanLocator:

HttpApplication.run(args, (routes, beans) -> {
    ItemService items = beans.getBean(ItemService.class);
    routes.GET("/items/{id}", (request, vars) -> HttpResponse.ok(items.find(vars.getLong("id"))));
});

Use build(String...) to configure the application before starting it, e.g. to choose the server when several are on the classpath and to customize its configuration:

HttpApplication.build(args)
    .server(NettyEmbeddedServer.class)
    .configure(NettyHttpServerConfiguration.class, netty -> netty.setMaxHeaderSize(16384))
    .routes(routes -> ...)
    .start();
